metadata.source: Ministry of Finance (DFS), MoA&FW, MoHUA, PFRDA, NABARD, SIDBI
metadata.exam_weightage: Extremely High (8-14 Questions across Mains shifts)

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)
schemes.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Services)
schemes.eligibility: Any individual above 10 years of age (minor account operated by guardian)
schemes.account_type: Basic Savings Bank Deposit (BSBD) Account with zero minimum balance

benefits.rupay_card: Free RuPay debit card with in-built accidental insurance
benefits.accidental_insurance: ₹2 Lakh for new accounts opened after August 28, 2018 (₹1 Lakh for accounts opened before August 28, 2018)
benefits.condition_for_claim: RuPay card must have been used at least once in 90 days prior to the accident date
benefits.overdraft_facility: Up to ₹10,000 (raised from ₹5,000 in 2018); OD up to ₹2,000 without any conditions
benefits.overdraft_age_limit: 18 to 65 years (revised from 18 to 60 years in 2018)
benefits.cheque_book: Not mandatory; can be issued if minimum balance conditions are maintained

schemes.exam_trap: Overdraft age limit was increased from 18-60 to 18-65 years, and max OD was doubled from ₹5,000 to ₹10,000. Accidental cover is ₹2 Lakh for accounts opened after Aug 28, 2018.

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)
schemes.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Services)
schemes.administering_entities: Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) and other life insurance companies partnering with banks
schemes.maximum_risk_cover_age: Up to age 55 years (subject to regular annual premium payment)
schemes.premium: ₹436 per annum (revised from ₹330/year effective June 1, 2022) auto-debited in one installment from bank account
schemes.risk_coverage: ₹2,00,000 (₹2 Lakh) in case of death of the insured due to ANY reason (natural or accidental)
schemes.lien_period: 30 days for new enrollments (claims due to accident are covered from day one)
schemes.exam_trap: Entry age is 18-50, but risk cover continues till age 55. Covers death due to ANY reason (unlike PMSBY which covers only accidental death/disability). Current annual premium is ₹436.

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)
schemes.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Services)
schemes.administering_entities: General insurance companies partnering with banks
schemes.premium: ₹20 per annum (revised from ₹12/year effective June 1, 2022) auto-debited annually

benefits.permanent_total_disability: ₹2,00,000 (loss of both eyes or loss of use of both hands or feet)
benefits.permanent_partial_disability: ₹1,00,000 (loss of sight of one eye or loss of use of one hand or foot)

schemes.exam_trap: Entry age is up to 70 years (higher than PMJJBY's 50 years). Premium is ₹20 per annum. Covers ONLY accidental death and permanent disability, NOT natural death.

schemes.name: Atal Pension Yojana (APY)
schemes.nodal_agency: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)
schemes.guaranteed_pension: ₹1,000, ₹2,00,00, ₹3,000, ₹4,000, or ₹5,000 per month based on contribution
schemes.government_guarantee: Central Government guarantees the minimum pension amount in case of fund underperformance
schemes.nominee_benefit: On death of subscriber, spouse receives same pension for life. On death of both, accumulated corpus is returned to the nominee.
schemes.taxpayer_restriction: From October 1, 2022, any citizen who is or has been an income-tax payer is NOT eligible to join APY.
schemes.exam_trap: Entry age is strictly 18 to 40 years. Taxpayers are banned since Oct 1, 2022. Minimum contribution period is 20 years (since entry is max 40 and pension begins at 60).

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY)
schemes.implementing_agency: Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency (MUDRA) Bank (subsidiary of SIDBI)
schemes.target_sector: Non-Corporate Small Business Sector (NCSBS) / micro enterprises in manufacturing, trading, and services

categories.loan_amount: Covering loans above ₹50,000 and up to ₹5,00,000 (₹5 Lakh)
Covering loans above ₹5,00,000 and up to ₹10,00,000 (₹10 Lakh)
Covering loans above ₹10,00,000 and up to ₹20,00,000 (₹20 Lakh) for entrepreneurs who previously availed and successfully repaid Tarun loans

schemes.collateral: NO collateral or third-party guarantee required for MUDRA loans up to ₹10 Lakh (covered under Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units - CGFMU)
schemes.exam_trap: MUDRA does NOT lend directly to individuals. It refinances commercial banks, RRBs, SFBs, MFIs, and NBFCs. Budget 2024 introduced Tarun Plus raising limit to ₹20 Lakh.

schemes.name: Stand-Up India Scheme
schemes.nodal_agency: Department of Financial Services (DFS), managed by SIDBI and NABARD
schemes.mandate: Each bank branch must facilitate bank loans between ₹10 Lakh and ₹1 Crore to at least one SC or ST borrower and at least one Woman borrower for setting up a greenfield enterprise.
schemes.eligible_sectors: Manufacturing, services, agri-allied activities, or the trading sector
schemes.non_individual_shareholding: At least 51% of shareholding and controlling stake must be held by either SC/ST or woman entrepreneur
schemes.margin_money: Up to 15% (can be provided in convergence with eligible Central/State schemes)
schemes.exam_trap: Mandate is AT LEAST ONE SC/ST and AT LEAST ONE Woman borrower PER BANK BRANCH. Loan range is ₹10 Lakh to ₹1 Crore. Applicable ONLY to greenfield (new) ventures.

schemes.name: PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi)
schemes.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)
schemes.implementing_agency: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
schemes.target_group: Street vendors vending in urban areas on or before March 24, 2020

tranches.amount: Working capital loan up to ₹10,000 (tenor 1 year)
Up to ₹20,000 upon timely repayment of first tranche
Up to ₹50,000 upon timely repayment of second tranche

schemes.interest_subvention: 7% per annum credited into borrower's bank account quarterly on timely repayment
schemes.digital_incentive: Cashback up to ₹1,200 per year (₹100/month) for digital transactions
schemes.exam_trap: PM SVANidhi is under Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (NOT Finance Ministry), but implemented through SIDBI. Offers 7% interest subvention and up to ₹50,000 in third tranche.

schemes.name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme
schemes.introduced: August 1998 (formulated by NABARD on recommendations of R.V. Gupta Committee)
schemes.purpose: Adequate and timely credit support from banking system under single window for agricultural operations and allied activities
schemes.credit_limit: Short term crop loan up to ₹3,00,000 (₹3 Lakh) at nominal 7% interest per annum
schemes.interest_subvention: 2% interest subvention to banks + 3% prompt repayment incentive (PRI) to farmers, resulting in effective interest rate of 4% per annum
schemes.allied_sectors_extension: Extended to Animal Husbandry, Dairy, and Fisheries in 2018-19 (limit up to ₹2 Lakh within overall ₹3 Lakh ceiling)
schemes.validity: Card valid for 5 years subject to annual review
schemes.collateral_free_limit: Collateral-free agricultural loans enhanced from ₹1 Lakh to ₹1.60 Lakh

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN)
schemes.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
schemes.nature_of_support: Central Sector Scheme (100% funded by Government of India)
schemes.financial_benefit: ₹6,000 per year transferred directly into bank accounts of landholder farmer families
schemes.installments: 3 equal installments of ₹2,000 every 4 months (April-July, August-November, December-March)
schemes.eligibility: All landholding farmer families having cultivable landholding in their names (subject to exclusion criteria like institutional landholders, income taxpayers, constitutional post holders)
schemes.exam_trap: PM-KISAN is 100% funded by Central Govt. Benefit is ₹6,000 in 3 installments of ₹2,000 via DBT. Excludes income-tax payers and institutional landholders.

schemes.name: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY)
schemes.launch_date: January 22, 2015 (launched under Beti Bachao Beti Padhao campaign in Panipat, Haryana)
schemes.nodal_department: Department of Posts & Department of Economic Affairs
schemes.account_opening_age: From birth till girl child attains 10 years of age
schemes.number_of_accounts: Maximum 1 account per girl child, and maximum 2 accounts per family (exception: twins/triplets)
schemes.deposit_limits: Minimum ₹250 per financial year; Maximum ₹1,50,000 (₹1.50 Lakh) per financial year
schemes.deposit_tenor: Deposits can be made for maximum 15 years from account opening date
schemes.maturity_period: Matures 21 years from account opening or on marriage of the girl child after attaining 18 years
schemes.tax_treatment: Exempt-Exempt-Exempt (EEE) status under Section 80C of Income Tax Act
schemes.partial_withdrawal: Up to 50% of balance at the end of preceding financial year allowed after age 18 or passing 10th standard for higher education

schemes.name: Mahila Samman Savings Certificate (MSSC)
schemes.investment_limit: Minimum ₹1,000; Maximum ₹2,00,000 (₹2 Lakh) in name of a woman or girl child
schemes.partial_withdrawal: Up to 40% of balance allowed after one year from opening date
schemes.exam_trap: Tenure is strictly 2 years. Maximum investment is ₹2 Lakh. Interest rate is fixed at 7.5% compounded quarterly.

exam_traps.trap: Believing PMJDY provides ₹5,000 overdraft to everyone automatically.
exam_traps.fact: Maximum OD is ₹10,000 (age 18-65). Only OD up to ₹2,000 is without conditions. The account must be operated satisfactorily for 6 months.
PMSBY covers ONLY accidental death and permanent disability. PMJJBY covers death due to ANY reason.

exam_traps.trap: Confusing APY entry age with PMJJBY.
exam_traps.fact: APY entry age is 18 to 40 years. PMJJBY entry age is 18 to 50 years. PMSBY entry age is 18 to 70 years.

exam_traps.trap: Assuming KCC crop loan limit is ₹5 Lakh.
exam_traps.fact: Standard KCC crop loan limit eligible for interest subvention is ₹3 Lakh (at 7% base, 4% with prompt repayment).
